notes.propulsion: Boost/sustain stage figures are AMRAAM-class estimates: the WPU-6/B motor's thrust history is not public. Constrained, not free: total impulse over propellant weight gives 247.8 s specific impulse against the ~245 s a solid HTPB motor achieves. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.2 and docs/VALIDATION.md (AIM-120 sources).
notes.mass: 6.294 + 4.121 slug = 91.9 + 60.1 kg = 152 kg, the published launch mass (Wikipedia, AIM-120 AMRAAM); the propellant load is the published motor's (156 lb motor, ~85% propellant, key.aero estimate). Two constraints, two numbers. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.3.
notes.reference_area_ft2: pi (0.584 / 2)^2: the published 178 mm body diameter.
notes.cd_vs_mach: ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT AIM-120 data: a generic slender-body shape (flat subsonic, transonic wave-drag peak, supersonic settle); its accuracy against the real missile is unknown, since no measured AIM-120 drag is public. The shape is what the sim teaches. Zero-lift, motor-off (coast) drag, used for the whole flight. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.4.
notes.normal_force: DERIVED, not measured: cn_alpha_per_deg_vs_mach and cn_max_vs_mach are computed by tools/fit/fit_normal_force.py from a component build-up (inputs: fit/normal_force_buildup.json) (NACA 1048 body, Jorgensen TN D-6996/D-7228 crossflow, NACA 1307 fins, from geometry measured off DTIC ADA355385 Fig 2; checked within ~10% of TM X-3310 supersonic). Values read off it: CN_max = the build-up's CN(alpha_max) at 25 000 ft; CN_alpha = the least-squares slope over alpha 0.5-10 deg with CN_max pinned. Rescaled to reference_area_ft2. Known gap: CN_max ~19-20 supersonic vs the IASGATG 2014 CFD study's 12-13 [S]. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.5.
notes.alpha_max_deg: 30 deg: fin flow separation in the IASGATG 2014 CFD study [S], the only source found. cn_max_vs_mach is the normal force at this angle, so changing it means refitting the tables. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.5.
notes.structural_g_limit: No published structural limit. 30 G is the IASGATG CFD study's test load, inside the 25-40 G spread of unsourced claims. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.5.
notes.seeker_mode: Inertial midcourse with datalink updates, then its own active seeker: how the AIM-120 is employed beyond visual range. See docs/REFERENCE.md 8.2.
notes.seeker_gimbal: fov_half_angle_deg and memory_coast_time_s are not published; chosen so a head-on shot never trips the cone. See docs/REFERENCE.md 8.1.
notes.active_seeker: X-band active seeker: f-16.net's AIM-120 article ('active X-band radar terminal seeker', 'high-power solid-state transmitter'); Jane's, quoted on the DCS forum, says I/J band (8-20 GHz), which covers X. No other AIM-120 seeker hardware figure is public. average_power_w 100: ESTIMATE. antenna_gain 148 (21.7 dBi): ESTIMATE, a 0.15 m dish inside the 7 in body at 60 % aperture efficiency, X-band. noise_figure_db 4 and integration_time_s 0.01 (one coherent look per 0.1 s sweep): ESTIMATES. pfa 1e-6: design convention; it sets the square-law threshold, ln(1/pfa) = 11.40 dB over noise. system_loss_db: FITTED, the only free parameter -- CALIBRATED by tools/fit/radar_budget.py so one look at a Swerling 1 5 m2 reference target (no aspect factor) detects with probability 0.5 at the commonly quoted ~10 nmi, in free space (fit/radar_fit.json); 9.3 nmi against the F-16 type's nose-on RCS estimate (3.78 m2). It absorbs the estimates above, so its 3.5 dB says little about the real seeker's losses. Acquisition needs confirm_hits of the last confirm_window sweeps (3 of 5): not published for the AIM-120; the commonly cited M-of-N baseline. At the nominal range each sweep is a coin flip, so 3 of 5 puts 50% acquisition exactly there instead of latching on the first scintillation spike. Doppler notch (the aircraft radar's rule seen from the missile, docs/REFERENCE.md 8.3 and 9.3): antenna_diameter_m 0.15, the dish behind the gain estimate above; beamwidth_factor 1.2, the radar's tapered-aperture estimate -> 1.2 lambda/D = 13.8 deg at 10 GHz, so the small dish sees ground far more often than the F-16's 4.3 deg beam; notch_velocity_threshold_mps 15: ESTIMATE, the radar's figure -- no AIM-120 clutter-filter figure is public. See docs/REFERENCE.md 8.3, 9.1 and 9.6.
notes.gravity_bias: Not a type field: every missile flies true PN (steered across the body axis, as lift must; true PN as defined in Palumbo et al., Basic Principles of Homing Guidance, JHU APL Tech. Digest 29(1), 2010, p. 29) with the gravity bias on. A tactical missile autopilot adds lift cancelling gravity's component across the body axis so guidance need not steer out the sag (gravity compensation; the bias is first-principles: cancel g across the body axis). Applies while guided, including after lock is lost. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.8.
notes.response_time_s: ESTIMATE: one first-order lag for the seeker, fins and airframe together, the single-time-constant guidance system of miss-distance analysis (Palumbo et al., Basic Principles of Homing Guidance, JHU APL Tech. Digest 29(1), 2010, p. 36 Eqs. 41-42: the loop approximated as one first-order lag whose time constant is the sum of the seeker, filter and flight-control lags). NOT published for the AIM-120. 0.35 s is the sum of a seeker LOS-rate lag of 0.15 s and an actuator lag of 0.2 s, both estimates, inside the 0.1-0.5 s autopilot time constants of Palumbo's Fig. 14 example (p. 37). Type only, not a scenario knob. See docs/REFERENCE.md 7.4.
notes.launch_turn_exit_deg: ESTIMATE, no source looked up: after an off-boresight launch the autopilot turns toward the line of sight at its available G until the target is within 15 deg of the velocity vector, then proportional navigation takes over. 15 deg = a third of the 45 deg seeker gimbal, leaving PN room to hold the target inside it. Without the turn, a launch with the target just inside the gimbal acquired at once and lost the target as PN turned too slowly. The type's value, read-only in a scenario and in the GUI; 0 = no launch turn. See docs/REFERENCE.md 6.9.
notes.loft: FITTED, not published: no public source gives an AIM-120 loft angle, threshold range or apex (Wikipedia, Missile lofting [S]: air-to-air lofts peak at 20 000-110 000 ft, and loft exists to save energy in thin air; Barrie, IISS [S]: the AIM-120D3 gained range by trajectory shaping). Free parameters start_range_nmi, full_range_nmi, max_climb_deg, fitted to our own model: the climb angle that gives the highest end-game speed at fixed launch ranges 8-50 nmi, head-on at 15 000/25 000/35 000 ft, shooter and target Mach 0.9, with the type's own 120 s time of flight; rounded to a straight line, within ~5% of the best speed at almost every probed point (worst -11%, 15 000 ft at 40 nmi). Below ~10 nmi climbing gains nothing; 20 deg is also where Rmax peaks. climb_time_constant_s 2: ESTIMATE, so the pull-up asks a few G rather than the airframe's limit. min_available_g 8: ESTIMATE, picked from a launch-zone sweep (4 / 8 G, and 80 000 / 100 000 ft ceilings): once burnt out the climb ends when the turn ceiling (docs/REFERENCE.md 6.5) falls under 8 G, else a loft from 45 000 ft climbs into air too thin to steer and loses ~25 nmi of reach; 8 G and an 80 000 ft ceiling gave the same zone. Only a missile still steering on the datalink lofts. See docs/REFERENCE.md - Loft.
notes.falloff_width_m: Width of the Pk-vs-miss-distance sigmoid around the kill radius. ESTIMATE: no public AIM-120 lethality curve exists. See docs/REFERENCE.md 12.
notes.arming_range_m: Straight-line distance from launch before the fuze can register a kill. Kept as a distance by design; a fuze that arms on a time delay is not modelled. 50 m is not a published AIM-120 figure. See docs/REFERENCE.md 12.5.
notes.self_destruct: NOT published for the AIM-120: no primary source gives a time of flight, battery life or self-destruct time. min_available_g 2.0 is first-principles: the end of useful flight is aerodynamic (Raero, VRS Support Wiki [S]); below 2 G only 1 G is left after holding the airframe up. It is checked only after burnout, since at launch the missile can have under 3 G while still accelerating. max_time_of_flight_s 120 is an estimate, chosen as a backstop above every hit the sim then produced (<= 86 s); with the loft hits fly up to 119 s and it binds (5 of 220 batch runs would hit at 200 s). Forum and game figures (~80 s presumed, War Thunder; 140 s DCS game file) were consulted, not used. Only max_time_of_flight_s is a teaching knob (missile_doctrine.self_destruct.max_time_of_flight_s). See docs/REFERENCE.md 12.7.
